newsitem.title: USA: NYSE weekly program trading averages 17.9 pct.
newsitem.headline: NYSE weekly program trading averages 17.9 pct.

text.p: The New York Stock Exchange said program trading averaged 17.9 percent of its average daily volume of 480.4 million shares, or 86.0 million shares, for the week of May 12-16.
Program trading accounted for an average of 18.7 percent of average daily volume of 531.8 million shares for the week of May 5-9.
Of the average 86.0 million shares during the week, buy programs accounted for an average 46.0 million shares, while sell programs accounted for an average 40.0 million daily.
In all markets, program trading averaged 108.6 million shares a day during the week of May 12-16.

Of the five member firms reporting the most program activity on the New York Stock Exchange, BNP Securities, Natwest, Morgan Stanley Solomon Brotherrs and Susquehanna Brokerage Services each executed all or most of its activity for customers.

Program trading executed by firms as agent, for non-member customers, amounted to 62.7 percent during the week, while volume executed as principal, for their own accounts, amounted to 35.7 percent of program volume from May 12-16.

Between May 12 and May 16, 33.3 percent of program trading volume executed by NYSE member firms was related to index arbitrage, while another 1.2 percent involved other derivative product-related strategies.
Program trading encompasses trading strategies involving the sale or purchase of a basket of at least 15 stocks with a value of $1 million or more the exchange said.
